stories.headline: Otters keep grinding out results
stories.detail: Kilburn have only lost once in five and are unbeaten in three, which has the Lockside Park crowd feeling they’re tough to shake. They’ve been drawing teams side to side and finding a late gap rather than forcing it.

stories.headline: Quintero fee looking like a steal
stories.detail: Rafa Quintero cost £2.4m in the summer and he’s already won fouls in dangerous spots, even if the goals have not quite flowed yet. Fans reckon the 21-year-old’s feet are causing defenders all sorts of trouble.

stories.headline: Fairweather still not ready
stories.detail: Back-up keeper Liam Fairweather is still sidelined and Tomas Brennan keeps the gloves for now. The Otters won’t rush the 34-year-old back after his latest setback in training.

stories.headline: Serrano bites back at the doubters
stories.detail: Manager Nico Serrano was blunt after the midweek draw, insisting his side do not need to turn into a long-ball team just because results have been tight. He says Kilburn’s passing game is the reason they’re sitting 8th, not the problem.

stories.headline: Ticket row over the Quay allocation
stories.detail: Kilburn fans are fuming at the small away allocation and the price jump for the Harbour City trip. One banner on matchday read: “Keep football for the people, not the pockets.”

stories.headline: Lockside Park plans get louder
stories.detail: The club keeps talking up a stand upgrade at Lockside Park, and the board says the move is tied to a better matchday income stream. Supporters just hope the extra money ends up on the pitch, not only in the office.

stories.headline: Pereira deal never got over the line
stories.detail: Kilburn tried to land a striker on deadline day, but the move collapsed after the fee climbed past £1.1m. Noah Pereira’s experience was the target, so fans are still wondering what might have been.

stories.headline: Whitcombe finally off the mark
stories.detail: Ollie Whitcombe has started to look like the poacher Kilburn paid for, with two goals in his last three appearances. The old gripe was that the build-up looked nice but the box had no bite.

stories.headline: Gulls flying after two straight wins
stories.detail: Harbour City have won their last two and look sharp on the break again, with Isaac Mwangi ending moves the way he should. They’re 5th now, and the away end is starting to dream bigger.

stories.headline: Mwangi price tag suddenly feels fair
stories.detail: Isaac Mwangi cost £3.1m and the talk was he’d need time, but his finishing has started to pay back the fee. Every run in behind now looks like money well spent.

stories.headline: Ferraro missing the bench again
stories.detail: Nico Ferraro is still out, so Harbour City are short on that burst of pace late in games. The 20-year-old’s been close, but not close enough for this trip.

stories.headline: Brennan hails the deep-block discipline
stories.detail: Manager Ruan Mercer praised his side’s patience, saying the low block and quick outlet are what make Harbour City awkward to face. He also swatted away questions about being too cautious, saying points matter more than style points.

stories.headline: Away fans chant for the counter
stories.detail: Harbour City supporters have been singing about “one pass and gone” ever since the last two wins. They think this team is at its best when it sits in and springs forward.

stories.headline: Sponsor boost lands before the derby
stories.detail: A new shirt sponsor has given Harbour City a tidy extra pay packet this month, and the club is already talking up January business. Fans just want some of that cash turned into another forward who can finish the breaks.

stories.headline: Last three meetings still sting
stories.detail: The last three meetings were Harbour City 2-1 Kilburn Athletic, last season, at The Quay; Kilburn Athletic 1-1 Harbour City, the season before, at Lockside Park; and Harbour City 0-0 Kilburn Athletic, the season before that, at The Quay. The memorable one is still the latest: Harbour City nicked it 2-1 after a late break, and Kilburn were left moaning about missing their chances.

stories.headline: Pike’s bargain move under the spotlight
stories.detail: Jordan Pike arrived for £900k and he’s had bright moments, but the rash side of his game still gets people talking. One loose challenge can undo all the good work in a hurry.

stories.headline: Bellandi marshals another shutout
stories.detail: Marco Bellandi has been leading the back line through a good spell, and Harbour City have looked much harder to open up. When they keep it tight, that front three only needs one clean break.
